rules.sentence: Metastatic bone disease may present with skeletal-related events such as pathological fractures, hypercalcemia, and metastatic extradural spinal cord compression [158].
Intracranial metastases may present with altered sensorium and signs of raised intracranial tension, such as headache, blurred vision, early morning nausea, and vomiting.

Common complications reported with radical nephrectomy include hemorrhage, wound infection, seroma, wound disruption, seroma, pneumothorax, sepsis, ileus, cardiac failure, renal events, peritonitis, and perihepatic collection.[157]
